To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

crude sugar ester extracts from Nicotiana species were found to be highly effective against the tobacco aphid, and that the crude sugar ester from N. gossie was found to be growth regulatory against the larvae of Helicoverpa.

crude sugar ester extracts from N. trigophylla and N. gosseii were highly effective in controlling tobacco aphid, whereas the same extracts from N. repanda and N. plambaginifolia showed moderate activity.
the sugar ester fractions of Nicotiana species are potential insecticides and insect growth regulators against M. nicotianae, H. armigara and H. armigere.

the development of new insect control strategies for the management of tobacco aphid and bud worm.
identification of the active components of sugar esters in Nicotiana sp., which can be used for development of botanical insecticides.
the development of new biopesticide formulations for the control of insect pests.

the sugar ester fractions of Nicotiana species could be used as an alternative to synthetic pesticides for controlling the tobacco aphid and bud worm in the future.
